chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Fadhl, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Ruh ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Like it, and he added to it: He said, 'I asked, 'What do you think if I give a wage for his writing?' He said, 'There is no harm, but this is how they used to do it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a scribe for writing a contract or document in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates compensating a scribe for drafting documents, grounding the ruling in the established customary practice (*urf*) of the community. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that the permissibility of transactional wages is often derived from prevailing social norms unless explicitly prohibited, thereby legitimizing professional services in commercial and legal contexts.
